# Results summary (generated by tools/summarize.py)

## Rate-distortion on iid N(0,1) (wasted bits = R - R*(D), lower is better)

Source: `results/rd_gaussian.json` (512k values). Pearl's numbers are read off their Fig. 5.

| point | Pearl's Fig. 5 | ours, no side info | ours, free exact per-vector norm | ours, incl. fp16 scale (the codec we ship) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PQ 2.75 bpv | 0.39 | 0.378 | 0.331 | 0.445 |
| PQ 3.75 bpv | 0.42 | 0.479 | 0.373 | 0.494 |
| TurboQuant-MSE 3 b | 0.56 | 0.558 (our re-run) | | |
| TurboQuant-MSE 4 b | 0.60 | 0.630 (our re-run) | | |
| NVFP4 4.5 bpv | 1.15 | 1.106 (our re-run) | | |
| FP8 e4m3 8 bpv | 2.65 | 2.762 (our re-run) | | |

HyperQuant E8 + Rice (variable rate, interpolated): 2.75 bpv -> 0.303, 3.75 bpv -> 0.265.
Voronoi (NestQuant) code at 2.75 bpv incl. scale: 0.529 vs ball 0.445.

## KL divergence from an FP8 KV cache, PG-19, Qwen/Qwen3-8B, 4 books x 16384 tokens

Reference: FP8 e4m3 with one fp32 scale per 128-value vector (8.25 bpv). `-kc` = our K mean-centering (softmax-invariant, free in the kernel). Model is not Pearl's.

| config | bits/value (K,V avg) | KL from FP8 (mean) | per book | PPL | Pearl's KL (GLM-5.3) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 | 16.000 | 0.0078 | 0.008, 0.008, 0.007, 0.009 | 16.88 |  |
| fp8-noscale | 8.000 | 0.0147 | 0.013, 0.016, 0.013, 0.017 | 16.90 |  |
| nvfp4 | 4.500 | 0.0551 | 0.052, 0.058, 0.053, 0.058 | 17.47 |  |
| nvfp4-kc | 4.500 | 0.0528 | 0.049, 0.057, 0.049, 0.057 | 17.38 |  |
| int4-g32 | 4.500 | 0.1180 | 0.109, 0.126, 0.103, 0.134 | 18.21 |  |
| tq-mse-3 | 3.125 | 1.0907 | 0.989, 1.101, 1.163, 1.110 | 41.94 |  |
| tq-mse-3-kc | 3.125 | 0.1502 | 0.133, 0.154, 0.132, 0.183 | 18.52 |  |
| tq-mse-2 | 2.125 | 2.4185 | 2.370, 2.512, 2.475, 2.317 | 143.35 |  |
| tq-mse-2-kc | 2.125 | 0.8275 | 0.739, 0.901, 0.736, 0.933 | 32.04 |  |

FP8 reference PPL 16.95. Pearl's FP8 noise floor is ~0.04 (nondeterminism); our runs are deterministic, bf16-vs-FP8 shows the FP8 error itself.
